_about: Sample translations for the i18n prototype (2026-10-16), made by Claude (Anthropic): es, de and ja in the prototype step, ru in the design step, with ../pipeline/style_packet.md and ../pipeline/glossary.json. Proof only: not reviewed by a native speaker, and the English and WOLF wording stay Nathanial's. Keys are the exact English msgids; 'context' says where each line shows, for the translator and the back-translator. 'marks' (added by the fix-2 step) gives each msgid's i18n marks, which `fill` writes as '#. i18n: ...' comments: who speaks, how the engineer appears (engineer=name, you or third) and what a %s holds when it is not the name (slot=key); the gender gate and the back-translation prompt read them (tools/i18n_tool.py, MARKS).

_revisions: 2026-10-16, after the overflow gate (tests/i18n_test.gd, I18n.overflows): de SETTINGS 'EINSTELLUNGEN' -> 'OPTIONEN' (the title button grew to 190 px in a 186 px slot); re-checked by an independent Codex back-translation (translations/codex_back.json, session 01a14409-6eb1-7db2-8ef1-f6f3714d953b). es NEW GAME stays 'NUEVA PARTIDA' (the usual term): it grows the button to 213 px of 186, into CONTINUAR; the shorter 'NUEVO JUEGO' still needs 193 px (both measured), so this one waits for a layout or wording decision and is pinned as the one known overflow in i18n_test.gd.

2026-10-16, design step: added ru (Russian), the Cyrillic proof among the top 10, with the style packet's ru rules: the engineer is never the subject of a past-tense verb (Russian past tense shows gender) and the name stays in the nominative (after a dash or a colon, or as the subject), so no case ending is needed for Rowan, Alex or Morgan; station plates are quoted in «» in their own nominative form; WOLF stays undeclined; the key token stays a Latin 'E:'. Breaker is 'рубильник' (a knife switch; 'автомат', the everyday word for a circuit breaker, also means an assault rifle, which a military base makes ambiguous).
